questions.question: Thermal radiation is energy emitted by matter due to:

options.A: Chemical reactions
options.B: Its temperature, in the form of electromagnetic waves

questions.question: Unlike conduction and convection, radiation heat transfer:

options.A: Requires a material medium

questions.question: The wavelength range of thermal radiation is approximately:

options.A: 0.1 to 100 micrometers

questions.question: Planck's law describes:

options.A: The spectral distribution of emissive power of a blackbody as a function of wavelength and temperature

questions.question: Wien's displacement law states that:

options.A: The wavelength of maximum emissive power is inversely proportional to absolute temperature
options.B: Emissive power is independent of temperature
options.C: The wavelength of maximum emission increases with temperature
options.D: Blackbody radiation has no peak wavelength

questions.question: According to Wien's displacement law, λmaxT = constant, where the constant is approximately:
The Stefan–Boltzmann law states that the total emissive power of a blackbody is proportional to:

options.A: T (absolute temperature)

questions.question: The Stefan–Boltzmann constant has a value of approximately:

options.A: 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/m²K⁴

questions.question: Kirchhoff's law of radiation states that, at thermal equilibrium:

options.A: Emissivity equals absorptivity for a surface at a given wavelength and temperature
options.D: Emissivity is always 1 for any surface

questions.question: Lambert's cosine law relates to:

options.A: The directional distribution of radiation intensity from a diffuse surface
options.C: The total energy balance of a blackbody

questions.question: A diffuse emitter, according to Lambert's law, emits radiation:

options.A: Only in the normal direction
options.B: Such that intensity is independent of direction

questions.question: The irradiation on a surface is defined as:

options.A: The rate at which radiation leaves a surface
options.B: The rate at which radiation is incident on a surface per unit area

questions.question: The radiosity of a surface is defined as:

options.A: The total rate of radiation leaving a surface (emitted + reflected) per unit area
options.B: The total radiation absorbed by a surface
options.C: The net heat transfer by conduction

questions.question: For an opaque surface, the sum of absorptivity (α) and reflectivity (ρ) equals:
For a semi-transparent surface, the energy balance of incident radiation involves:

options.A: Absorptivity and reflectivity only
options.B: Absorptivity, reflectivity, and transmissivity, summing to 1

questions.question: Emissive power of a surface is defined as:

options.A: Rate of radiant energy emitted by a surface per unit area
options.B: Rate of radiant energy absorbed by a surface
options.C: Rate of heat conduction through a surface

questions.question: The radiation emitted by a real surface compared to a blackbody at the same temperature is:

options.A: Always greater
options.C: Always less than or equal to the blackbody emission

questions.question: The fraction of blackbody radiation within a specific wavelength band is found using:

options.A: Radiation function / blackbody fraction tables (λT tables)

questions.question: The sun's surface can be approximated as a blackbody radiating at approximately:
As the temperature of a blackbody increases, the peak wavelength of its emission spectrum:

options.A: Increases

questions.question: Spectral emissive power refers to:

options.A: Total emissive power integrated over all wavelengths
options.B: Emissive power per unit wavelength at a given wavelength
options.C: Emissive power per unit area only
options.D: Emissive power in the visible spectrum only

questions.question: The fundamental radiation laws (Planck's, Wien's, Stefan–Boltzmann's) are derived specifically for:

options.A: Real (gray) surfaces

questions.question: Radiation intensity I is defined as:

options.A: Rate of radiant energy per unit solid angle per unit projected area

questions.question: Integration of Planck's spectral distribution over all wavelengths yields:

options.A: Wien's displacement law constant
options.B: The Stefan–Boltzmann law (total emissive power ∝ T⁴)

questions.question: Solar radiation reaching Earth is primarily in which spectral range?

options.A: Ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared (short wavelength)

questions.question: A blackbody is defined as a surface that:

options.A: Absorbs all incident radiation and reflects none

questions.question: A blackbody, at any given temperature and wavelength, emits:

options.A: Less radiation than any other real surface
options.B: The maximum possible radiation among all surfaces

questions.question: A practical approximation of a blackbody is:

options.A: A polished mirror
options.B: A small opening (cavity) in an isothermal enclosure

questions.question: Emissivity (ε) of a surface is defined as the ratio of:

options.A: Emissive power of the surface to that of a blackbody at the same temperature

questions.question: For a blackbody, emissivity is:
A gray body is defined as a surface whose:

options.A: Emissivity varies strongly with wavelength
options.B: Emissivity is constant (independent of wavelength) over the relevant spectrum

questions.question: For a gray, diffuse surface, Kirchhoff's law implies:

options.A: Emissivity equals absorptivity (ε = α) at a given temperature
options.B: Emissivity is always greater than absorptivity

questions.question: A white (perfectly reflective) surface has:

options.A: Emissivity and absorptivity equal to 1
options.B: Emissivity and absorptivity equal to 0, reflectivity equal to 1

questions.question: Most real engineering surfaces behave approximately as:

options.A: Perfect blackbodies

questions.question: The emissivity of a surface generally depends on:

options.A: Surface material, finish/roughness, and temperature
options.C: Only the shape of the object
options.D: Nothing; it is a universal constant

questions.question: Polished metallic surfaces typically have:

options.A: Very high emissivity, close to 1

questions.question: Non-metallic surfaces such as painted or oxidized surfaces typically have emissivity values that are:

options.A: Close to zero

questions.question: The emissive power of a gray body at temperature T is given by:

options.A: E = εσT⁴

questions.question: A surface with directionally uniform emissivity (intensity independent of direction) is called:

options.A: A specular surface

questions.question: Selective surfaces (e.g., solar absorber coatings) are designed to have:

options.A: High absorptivity for solar (short) wavelengths and low emissivity for long (thermal) wavelengths
options.B: Equal absorptivity and emissivity at all wavelengths

questions.question: The concept of a gray body simplifies radiation calculations by assuming:

options.A: Properties vary with wavelength exactly like a blackbody
options.B: Radiative properties (ε, α, ρ) are constant over the wavelength spectrum of interest

questions.question: Which of the following emissivity values would be physically impossible for a real surface?
The emissivity of human skin in the infrared range is approximately:

options.A: 0.97 (close to a blackbody)

questions.question: For a gray, opaque, diffuse surface (α = absorptivity, ρ = reflectivity), which relation holds?

options.A: α + ρ = 1

questions.question: The total emissivity of a surface, used in engineering calculations, is obtained by:

options.A: Integrating the spectral emissivity weighted by the blackbody spectral distribution over all wavelengths
options.B: Taking the emissivity at only one specific wavelength
options.D: Ignoring wavelength dependence with no averaging

questions.question: Net radiant heat exchange between a small gray surface and large surroundings (treated as a blackbody) is given by:

options.A: Q = εσA(Ts⁴ − Tsurr⁴)

questions.question: In many practical heat transfer problems, surrounding surfaces are approximated as blackbodies because:

options.A: They are usually small compared to the object
options.B: Large enclosures approximate blackbody behavior for radiation exchange with a small object inside
options.D: It simplifies calculations with no physical justification

questions.question: A surface with emissivity close to zero would appear nearly:

options.A: Perfectly black

questions.question: The gray-body assumption breaks down significantly when:

options.A: The surface's spectral emissivity varies strongly with wavelength over the relevant range

questions.question: The emissive power of a blackbody integrated over all wavelengths is given directly by:

options.A: Stefan–Boltzmann law: Eb = σT⁴
options.D: Planck's law only, with no integration

questions.question: The shape factor (view factor) F12 between two surfaces represents:

options.A: The fraction of radiation leaving surface 1 that is intercepted directly by surface 2
options.D: The total heat transfer coefficient between surfaces

questions.question: Shape factor values always lie in the range:

options.A: −1 to 1

questions.question: The reciprocity relation for shape factors is given by:

options.B: F12 = F21 always, regardless of areas

questions.question: The summation rule for shape factors from surface i in an enclosure with N surfaces states:

options.A: The sum of Fij for j = 1 to N equals 1
options.C: The sum of Fij equals N
options.D: Fij is always equal for all j

questions.question: The shape factor of a surface with respect to itself (Fii) is zero when the surface is:

options.A: Concave

questions.question: For a concave surface, the self-view factor Fii is:

options.A: Always zero
options.B: Greater than zero, since the surface can 'see' part of itself

questions.question: Shape factor algebra is used to:

options.A: Determine shape factors for complex geometries by combining known shape factors of simpler sub-surfaces

questions.question: For two infinite parallel plates (very large compared to their separation), the shape factor F12 is:
For a small object completely enclosed within a large cavity, the shape factor from the small object to the cavity (F12) is:

options.D: Equal to the ratio of areas

questions.question: Shape factor charts/graphs are typically used to determine F12 for standard geometries such as:

options.A: Coaxial parallel disks, perpendicular rectangles with a common edge, etc.
options.D: They are never needed; shape factors are always derived analytically from scratch

questions.question: In a three-surface enclosure, the number of shape factors that must be determined directly (before using reciprocity and summation rules) is generally:

options.A: Nine
options.B: Fewer than the total possible combinations, since many can be derived using reciprocity and summation

questions.question: The shape factor between two surfaces depends on:

options.A: Their geometry, relative orientation, and distance between them

questions.question: If surface 1 cannot 'see' surface 2 at all (no direct line of sight), the shape factor F12 is:
The symmetry rule in shape factor algebra is used when:

options.A: Two or more surfaces are geometrically symmetric, simplifying shape factor relations
options.B: There is no symmetry at all

questions.question: For a flat surface facing a hemisphere that completely encloses it, the shape factor from the flat surface to the hemisphere is:
The view factor is dimensionless because it represents:

options.A: A ratio (fraction) of radiant energy leaving one surface that reaches another
options.D: An area ratio unrelated to radiation

questions.question: Shape factors are purely a function of:

options.A: Geometry only (independent of surface temperature or radiative properties)

questions.question: For two concentric spheres (a complete two-surface enclosure), the self-view factor F11 for the inner sphere is:

options.A: 0 (since it is convex and cannot see itself)

questions.question: In radiative heat exchange network analysis, shape factor is used along with emissivity to determine:

options.A: Thermal conductivity
options.B: The net radiative heat exchange between surfaces

questions.question: For two identical, parallel, directly-opposed finite rectangular plates, the shape factor generally:

options.A: Increases as the separation distance decreases (plates closer together)
options.C: Decreases as the plates get closer

questions.question: Shape factor determination for complex 3D geometries is often done using:

options.A: Hottel's crossed-string method (for 2D) or numerical/graphical methods
options.B: Only direct measurement with a thermometer

questions.question: Hottel's crossed-string method is primarily applicable to:

options.A: Two-dimensional (long) geometries

questions.question: The shape factor from a differential area element to a finite surface is determined by:

options.A: Integrating the shape factor relation (involving cosines of angles and distance) over the finite surface

questions.question: For a two-surface enclosure where surface 1 is flat and completely enclosed by surface 2, F21 is given by:

options.A: A1F12/A2 (from reciprocity)
options.C: F12, since F12 always equals F21

questions.question: Shape factor concepts are essential in radiation network analysis because they allow calculation of:

options.A: Energy exchange fractions between multiple radiating surfaces in an enclosure

questions.question: The electrical network analogy for radiation heat transfer relates radiative heat flow to:

options.A: Current flow through a network of resistances, analogous to Ohm's law

questions.question: In the radiation network analogy, the 'surface resistance' of a gray, diffuse, opaque surface is given by:
For a blackbody (ε = 1), the surface resistance in the radiation network is:

options.A: Infinite

questions.question: In the radiation network analogy, the 'space resistance' (geometric resistance) between two surfaces is given by:
In the radiation network analogy, the driving potential (analogous to voltage) is represented by:

options.A: Blackbody emissive power (Eb = σT⁴) at nodes, with radiosity (J) as intermediate nodes

questions.question: For radiative heat exchange between two large parallel gray plates, the network consists of:

options.A: Two surface resistances and one space resistance in series

questions.question: Net radiative heat transfer between two infinite parallel gray plates (emissivities ε1, ε2) is given by:
Radiation shields are thin, high-reflectivity (low-emissivity) sheets placed between two radiating surfaces to:

options.A: Increase heat transfer between them
options.B: Reduce the net radiative heat transfer between them
options.C: Have no effect on heat transfer

questions.question: A radiation shield works by:

options.A: Absorbing and re-emitting radiation at a lower rate, adding additional resistance to the radiation network
options.B: Perfectly transmitting all radiation without any effect
options.D: Increasing the shape factor between the two surfaces

questions.question: For two identical parallel plates (emissivity ε) separated by a single radiation shield (also emissivity ε), the heat transfer rate becomes approximately:

options.A: The same as without the shield
options.B: About half of what it would be without any shield

questions.question: For n identical radiation shields placed between two parallel plates, each with emissivity equal to that of the plates, the heat transfer rate is reduced approximately by a factor of:

options.A: 1/(n+1), compared to the no-shield case
options.C: Unaffected by the number of shields

questions.question: Using multiple low-emissivity shields rather than one shield to reduce radiation heat transfer:

options.A: Is less effective than a single shield
options.B: Progressively reduces net heat transfer further with each added shield
options.C: Has no additional benefit beyond one shield

questions.question: Radiation shields are commonly used in applications such as:

options.A: Thermos flasks, spacecraft thermal control, and cryogenic storage systems

questions.question: For effective radiation shielding, the shield material should ideally have:

options.A: High emissivity to maximize absorption
options.B: Low emissivity (highly reflective) on both surfaces to minimize radiative emission
options.C: High thermal conductivity, with no concern for emissivity

questions.question: In the radiation network with a shield, the total resistance between two surfaces is given by:

options.A: The sum of all surface and space resistances in the series network, including the shield's two surface resistances
options.B: Just the resistance of the shield alone
options.D: The average of the individual resistances

questions.question: A superinsulation system typically uses:

options.A: A single thick metal plate
options.B: Multiple layers of radiation shields separated by vacuum or low-conductivity spacers
options.D: Only a single layer of insulation with high emissivity

questions.question: A radiation shield's own temperature, once in steady state between two surfaces, settles at a value:

options.A: Equal to the hotter surface's temperature
options.B: Equal to the colder surface's temperature
options.C: Between the temperatures of the two bounding surfaces

questions.question: The effectiveness of a radiation shield increases as its emissivity:

options.A: Increases toward 1

questions.question: For radiation shields with different emissivities on each side (ε3,1 and ε3,2), the overall resistance calculation must account for:

options.A: Both surface resistances of the shield individually, as they can differ
options.B: Only one resistance value, assuming it is the same on both sides
options.D: Only the space resistance, ignoring the shield's surface properties

questions.question: The primary purpose of using the electrical analogy for radiation networks is to:

options.A: Allow radiative heat transfer problems to be solved using familiar series/parallel resistance network techniques
options.B: Convert radiative heat transfer into electrical energy
options.D: Eliminate the need for shape factors entirely

questions.question: In a three-surface radiation enclosure problem with a reradiating (insulated) surface, that surface is modeled in the network as:

options.A: A node with zero net heat flow (floating node) connected by resistances to other surfaces
options.D: An open circuit with infinite resistance to all other nodes

questions.question: Space resistance between two surfaces in a radiation network decreases when:

options.A: The shape factor F12 decreases
options.B: The areas and shape factor (A1F12) increase, improving the view between surfaces
options.C: The surfaces are far apart with a poor view

questions.question: Radiation shielding is particularly important in reducing heat loss in:

options.A: Cryogenic fluid storage (e.g., liquid nitrogen/helium dewars) where even small heat gains matter greatly

questions.question: The combined use of shape factor, surface resistance, and space resistance in a radiation network allows engineers to determine:

options.A: Net radiative heat exchange in multi-surface enclosures systematically

questions.question: Compared to a surface with no shield, inserting a radiation shield between two radiating surfaces:

options.A: Always increases the effective thermal resistance of the radiative path, reducing net heat transfer
options.B: Always decreases the effective thermal resistance
options.C: Has no effect on thermal resistance
options.D: Converts radiative heat transfer entirely into conduction
